title: Does Born Rule Imply Unitarity of Time Evolution in Quantum Mechanics?
abstract: The Born rule for computing probabilities of the outcomes of measurements is an indispensable ingredient of quantum mechanics. The standard textbook description of this rule gives the impression that it implies the unitarity of time evolution. This view relies on the argument that unless the dynamics is unitary, the probabilities of finding all possible outcomes of a measurement do not add up to 1, i.e., the total probability is not conserved. We show that this argument is flawed, and that the general expression for the Born rule ensures the conservation of total probabilities even when the dynamics of a quantum system is not unitary. This applies to the dynamics of ensembles of quantum systems in both pure and mixed states. We discuss the status of the local conservation of probabilities and the arguments against the plausibility of non-unitary time evolutions that are based on the identification of the Hamiltonian operator with the energy observable.
summary: This paper investigates whether the Born rule inherently requires that quantum time evolution be unitary. It demonstrates that the standard textbook argument is flawed because probability conservation can hold even for non-unitary dynamics when a generalized form of the Born rule is employed. The findings suggest a necessary distinction between local probability conservation and global probability normalization in open or non-Hermitian systems.
main_problem: The central question is whether the Born rule, which governs measurement probabilities, necessitates that quantum time evolution must be unitary.
main_result: The standard argument linking the Born rule to unitarity is flawed; probability conservation can be maintained even with non-unitary dynamics by using a generalized form of the Born rule. The requirement for local probability conservation in position space suggests Hermiticity but does not prove it.
method: The analysis involves deriving and comparing different forms of the Born rule for pure and mixed states, extending to non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, and analyzing continuity equations for probability densities.
model_or_system: The paper considers general quantum mechanical systems in a complex Hilbert space, ranging from pure state evolution governed by $\psi$ to ensemble dynamics described by density operators $ho$. It examines the implications of measurement probabilities across both unitary and non-unitary time evolutions.
key_observables: Probability of measuring eigenvalue $P_{Born}$, total probability conservation ($\sum P = 1$), localization probability density $\varrho_{px, tq}$, and expectation values of observables $\langle \psi | p_O | \psi angle$.
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to whether the Hamiltonian is Hermitian or if the state vector/density operator is normalized.
main_assumptions: The standard argument assumes a normalized state vector ($\|\psi\|=1$) and that all physical observables must have real expectation values, which leads to assumptions about Hermiticity.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes; the analysis relies on mathematical derivations of probability formulas (Eq. 12, Eq. 19, Eq. 29) and continuity equations (Eq. 52).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first presenting the standard flawed argument linking Born rule to unitarity. It then generalizes the Born rule for non-unitary dynamics using scaling factors. Finally, it contrasts this with local conservation laws in position space, which suggest Hermiticity but are shown to be distinct from the general probability conservation.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles foundational issues regarding the measurement postulate and time evolution structure, which underpin all quantum dynamics models used in AMO physics and open system descriptions.
